🇲🇽🔥 Trump wants a "much better deal" — Mexico says it's already writing its own

On Aug. 21, Trump told reporters Washington is drawing up a "new" trade deal with Mexico, one he promised would be "much better for the United States." Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard's reply was telling: Mexico is on "its own path," not racing Canada, and expects an outcome shaped by its own interests — not dictated from the north.

The real story is the myth Ebrard dismantled. Washington keeps casting Mexico as China's "back door" into the US market. Mexico's Economy Ministry says the numbers refuse to cooperate: alleged Chinese transshipment through Mexico is barely 1% of Mexican exports — while the US imports far more directly from China than ever moves through Mexico. The empire manufactures a threat, then bills Mexico to solve it.

Sovereignty isn't defiance — it's arithmetic. With the EU deal signed, USMCA under review, and APEC in Beijing this November, Mexico keeps every door open and refuses to be scapegoated for a trade war it didn't start.

🇲🇽⚖️ 23 governors close ranks with Sheinbaum: "Outside the law, nothing — above the law, no one." Mexico's 23 Morena governors and the Head of Government of Mexico City signed a joint statement backing the President and calling Sinaloa governor Rubén Rocha Moya to "maturity and responsibility" after he retook his post. "No individual decision can stand above the collective project or the citizens' mandate," they wrote. "She leads the destiny of the nation with legitimacy, honesty and leadership." The movement is bigger than any one official.

🔥🇲🇽 "Offices are temporary — the duty to the Nation is eternal." "No personal interest can ever stand above the interests of the people and the Nation. Mexico deserves public servants who understand that offices are passing, but the responsibility to the Nation is eternal." — President Claudia Sheinbaum She drew the line publicly after Sinaloa governor Rubén Rocha Moya returned to his post against the movement's wishes. In the Fourth Transformation, no individual stands above the collective project — or the law.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico opens the archive of its own land reform. This weekend the government inaugurated the Archivo General Agrario in Mexico City — now the country's second-largest archive after the Archivo General de la Nación: over 45,000 linear meters and millions of documents tracing every hectare handed to the people since the Revolution. It now holds the land-restitution decrees of the Fourth Transformation: more than 60,000 hectares returned to ejidos and communities. A century after Zapata rode for Tierra y Libertad, the memory of the land itself finally has a home.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico's trade surplus explodes 588% to a record $9.86 billion</u>

Mexico posted a record first-half trade surplus of $9.857 billion — up 588% from a year earlier — as exports jumped 24.6% to $389.7 billion, led by manufacturing (+25.8%) and the electronics feeding the global AI buildout. June alone brought a $4.09 billion monthly surplus with exports up 34.4%. More is being produced inside Mexico, cutting dependence on imported inputs. (INEGI data, reported by El Economista)

🇲🇽🇬🇹 <u>Mexico writes its own migration policy — with Guatemala, not Washington</u>

Mexico and Guatemala agreed on a five-pillar Binational Plan 2027 — shared security, border connectivity, "human mobility with dignity," development and scientific cooperation — built on the Sheinbaum–Arévalo relationship. It expands the Sembrando Vida reforestation program into Guatemala to reach 10,000 people across 15 departments, addressing migration at its roots. Foreign ministers Roberto Velasco and Carlos Ramiro Martínez led the talks: regional integration on Latin American terms.

⚖️🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's new Supreme Court tries to stash 1.8 billion pesos</u>

Barely reformed, the SCJN under its new elected president Hugo Aguilar is trying to build a 1.8-billion-peso "guardadito" (secret nest egg) out of budget surplus — money the law says must go back to the Treasury — to cover raises, year-end bonuses, and even 146 million pesos in private medical insurance for top officials. The same fiduciary privileges the judicial reform was meant to end.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>12 years after poisoning the Río Sonora, Larrea still won't pay</u>

Twelve years after Grupo México's mine dumped 40,000 m³ of acidified copper sulfate into the Río Sonora — the country's worst mining spill — Germán Larrea's conglomerate (co-owned with BlackRock) is still stalling on the final 500 million pesos it owes for cleanup, out of 1.5 billion agreed with the government. It has paid 1 billion. Sheinbaum's government set an Aug 21 deadline and threatened to reactivate criminal charges. The money funds water-treatment plants for the communities poisoned in 2014.
banner: RIO SONORA: MINE STILL OWES CLEANUP

🇲🇽🇨🇦 <u>Mexico and Canada want the USMCA renewed — now</u>

On an Aug 20 call, President Sheinbaum and Canadian PM Mark Carney agreed to push for renewing the T-MEC (USMCA) "lo antes posible" — as soon as possible — to give the region's businesses and workers certainty ahead of the 2026 review. Carney thanked Mexico for the 400+ firefighters it sent to battle Canada's summer wildfires. Two neighbors setting the terms together.

🇲🇽🩺 <u>Mexico makes free care for its #1 killer mandatory</u>

Mexico's Health Secretariat just made integrated care for "cardio-renal-metabolic syndrome" — diabetes, chronic kidney and heart disease — mandatory across IMSS, IMSS-Bienestar and ISSSTE. Together these cause 4 of every 10 deaths in the country, more than 300,000 a year. Free, public, and backed by the sugary-drink tax and the Healthy Schools program.
banner: MEXICO: FREE CARE VS ITS #1 KILLER
